title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Payment Cancellation and Reissue Terms
content:
A payment on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is cancelled only by reference to the single original payment it reverses, recorded as the original payment on the cancellation, and the cancelled amount equals that payment's amount.

## Cancellation reasons and what follows

| Situation | Cancellation reason | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| A direct deposit returned by the receiving bank | Returned by bank | Reissued through the returned-deposit reissue method |
| A paper check reported lost or stolen, once the waiting period has run | Lost or stolen check | Reissued through the payment method in force |
| A payment issued for a week later found not payable, before the funds were released | Issued in error | Not reissued |
| A payment stopped because the claim is under fraud review | Fraud stop | Not reissued unless the hold is released |

Once funds were released for a week later found not payable, the amount is pursued as an overpayment instead of a cancellation.

## Lost or stolen paper checks

A paper check reported lost or stolen may be stopped only on or after the lost-check waiting period after the check's issue date. The waiting period is counted in business days (Monday through Friday excluding state holidays) starting the business day after the check's issue date. The issue date read is the payment's issue date on the claim's payment history.

Boundary, for a 10-business-day waiting period on a check issued on a Monday with no state holiday in the following two weeks:

| Day of the stop request | Business days counted after the issue date | Stop allowed |
|---|---|---|
| Friday of the following week | 9 | No |
| Monday two weeks after the issue date | 10 | Yes |

## Single cancellation and balance effects

- A payment may be cancelled only once.
- Cancellation credits the cancelled amount back to the remaining benefit balance, a reissue debits it again, and a reissued payment is not charged to employers a second time.

### Hypothetical illustration

A 300.00 direct deposit returned by the bank is cancelled for 300.00, raising the remaining balance by 300.00; the reissue by the returned-deposit method debits 300.00 again, and employers are not charged for the reissue.
